correctness.rationale: The cited theorem identifies the smooth-locus Poincare polynomial with a monomial shift of the Schroeder polynomial graded by diagonal-step count. Deleting k diagonal steps is a bijection to a Dyck path of semilength n-k together with a weak placement of k diagonals among its 2(n-k)+1 gaps, giving binomial(2n-k,k) C_{n-k}. The resulting consecutive-coefficient quotient is exact. Its cross-multiplied difference is the quadratic 2k^2-4nk+n^2-n, whose only root in the coefficient range is rho_n=n-sqrt(n(n+1)/2). This proves strict increase/decrease and shows that a tie exists exactly when the triangular number n(n+1)/2 is square; the standard completion of the square gives the Pell equation. The packaged checker independently reconstructs the source recurrence and verifies the formulas on a large finite range without using those checks as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The smooth locus is a natural geometric stratum of a standard singular flag degeneration, and its Poincare polynomial is a primary topological invariant. The theorem gives the exact location and multiplicity of its largest graded piece for every rank, rather than only total Euler characteristic or a recurrence. The infinite exceptional set is structurally sharp: a two-term top plateau occurs precisely at square-triangular dimensions, equivalently a Pell orbit, beginning with the nontrivial case n=8. This turns a known Schroeder-polynomial description into a precise global phase law for the cohomological profile.
